title: HE LEFT THE TABLE.
paragraphs:
Coins still clinked.
Ink still wet on the ledger.
Power still in his pocket.
In Gospel of Matthew 9, a man named Matthew is sitting at a tax booth. Not just working. Thriving.

Tax collectors weren’t misunderstood introverts.
They were collaborators.
Agents of Rome.
Profiting off their own people.

Dirty money.
Clean robes.
Empty soul.
And Jesus walks straight to the table.

No debate.
No lecture.
No résumé review.

Why not a synagogue leader?
Why not a polished rabbi-in-training?

Because grace doesn’t knock on the door of the worthy.
It invades the booth of the compromised.

Some scholars interpret Matthew’s immediate response as a sign that Jesus had prior interactions with him. Maybe.
But Scripture says this clearly:

From comfort.
From income.
From identity.

Jesus doesn’t just call Matthew.
He goes to Matthew’s house.
Sits at Matthew’s table.
Eats with Matthew’s friends.

Religious leaders whisper,
“Why does your Teacher eat with them?”
Because mercy tastes better than self-righteousness.

Jesus answers:
“I desire mercy, not sacrifice… For I came not to call the righteous, but sinners.” (Matthew 9:13)
That’s the Gospel in one sentence.

Not the polished.
Not the impressive.
Sinners.
Let me speak to the one gripping your own “table” right now.

The relationship that feeds your ego.
The habit that funds your comfort.
The identity built on compromise.
But what you leave is nothing compared to Who you gain.

Matthew left coins.
He gained Christ.

He left a booth.
He received a calling.

He left a corrupt ledger.
He wrote a Gospel.
Here’s the open loop I promised you:
The man who once extracted money became a gift to the Church.

He doesn’t just forgive your past.
He repurposes it.
Jesus is still walking past tables today.

Not when you clean up.
Not when you feel worthy.

Because the One calling you is on His way to a cross—
where He will leave heaven’s glory,
stretch out His hands,
and pay your debt in full.

And if He can turn a tax collector into an evangelist—
He can turn your mess into a message.
